data.narrative:
Dimensional Energy is a Series A climate and energy company founded by Tobias Hanrath, Jason Salfi, David Erickson, and Clayton D. Poppe, having raised $25.4M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a peer universe of nine comparable companies in the Climate & Energy sector, including one public comparable (LNZA) and eight private peers such as Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix.

Only one valuation method proved applicable to the dataset. The Stage-Progression approach, using total capital raised as a baseline proxy, applies a 2.0x multiplier typical of Series A progression to subsequent funding rounds. This method yields an implied valuation of $51M. A peer-median approach could not be reliably executed due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparable datapoints within the narrowly filtered Climate & Energy set, though eight same-sector peers exist in the broader universe.

The triangulation analysis supports a valuation range of $43M to $58M, with a median point of $51M. This range reflects methodological constraints: reliance on a single quantitative anchor (stage-progression) introduces material uncertainty around the terminal valuation. Key sensitivities include the appropriate step-up multiplier for this stage and subsector, the relevance of the peer universe given climate tech's heterogeneity, and the degree to which total raised approximates pre-money valuation. Investors should treat this range as illustrative pending access to comparable transaction multiples or detailed financial performance data.
